4.4 Linkage to Financial Statements
Below is a table presenting how a material topic may materially impact our financial statements (Profit or Loss, Balance Sheet,
or similar) if certain thresholds are crossed:
Material Topic Potential Financial Impact Areas
Climate Risk & Resilience Statement of Profit or Loss: Loan loss provisions related to drought/flood-exposed
agricultural clients. Potential increased operating costs due to adaptation measures.
Statement of Financial Position: Possible revaluation or early write-down of financed
assets in high-carbon sectors if transition policies tighten.
Cybersecurity & Data Privacy Statement of Profit or Loss: Fines, legal fees, and incident response costs following a
data breach. Increased cybersecurity spending to enhance defences.
Statement of Financial Position: Increased provisions for liabilities in case of major
litigation related to data breaches.
Financial Inclusion & Accessibility Statement of Comprehensive Income: Fee income growth driven by newly served
market segments and synergy with digital transformation .
Statement of Financial Position: Increase in loans and advances to customers.
Ethical Banking & Responsible Statement of Profit or Loss: Fines resulting from regulatory breaches.
Lending Balance Sheet Items: Possible increase in loan loss provisions if lending practices are
deemed irresponsible.
Profit & Loss: Potential cost savings from reduced compliance breaches or lawsuits.
Reputational Risk (Indirect): Impacts on deposit base, share price, and customer
acquisition if unethical practices are publicized.
Community Investment & Social Long-Term Financial Health: Building trust and loyalty among local communities,
Impact which can stabilize deposits, improve access to funding, and bolster brand reputation
(contributes to long-term sustainability, but not directly quantifiable in the short term).
4.5 Justification for Changes from 2023
We shall revisit our material topics after every two years to reflect evolving regulations, stakeholder concerns, and the Bank’s
strategic direction. Significant changes include:
2023 Topic 2024 Topic Reason for Change
Climate Change Mitigation Climate Risk & Resilience Emphasized the financial dimension of climate
risk (both physical and transition), plus the Bank’s
resilience strategies.
Digital Banking Customer Experience & Digital Expanded scope includes improved user interfaces,
Transformation data protection, and the full lifecycle of digital
engagement (beyond channel access).
Job Creation & Employee Human Capital Development Broader category focused on leadership, training,
Welfare and well-being. Reflects new internal feedback
on management-level skill development and
performance review management.
Sustainable Investing Sustainable Finance & Green Elevates the Bank’s role in financing renewable
Investments energy, climate adaptation, and sustainability-
driven lending
